title: Unto Thy Temple, God of Love
description: Unto Thy Temple, God of Love in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 10, “"It is Good to be Here."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Un-to Thy tem-ple, God of love, Once more we come with will-ing feet, To raise our thoughts this world a-bove, And Thy pa-ter-nal bless-ing meet.

lines: Unto Thy temple, God of love,
Once more we come with willing feet,
To raise our thoughts this world above,
May all Thy purest presence feel,
And silent keep each vain desire;
With humble hearts before Thee kneel,
May all be bound in bonds more true
To Thee, who art our life and light,
That through each path which we pursue,
We still may keep Thy love in sight.
And may we, when the day shall close,
Review its course without a fear;
And, nearer heaven than when it rose,
Feel it is good to have been here.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
